Enum Class LinearLayout.JustifyContent

public static enum LinearLayout.JustifyContent extends Enum<LinearLayout.JustifyContent>
Defines how a LinearLayout will distribute space between and around content items along the main axis.

  • Enum Constant Details

    • STRETCH

      public static final LinearLayout.JustifyContent STRETCH
      The children will be stretched to the containers edges along the main axis, no space will be left on the start and end of the container. The children will grow as much as specified using LinearLayout.withWeight(double, Widget) or LinearLayout.expanded(Widget).

    • START

      public static final LinearLayout.JustifyContent START
      Place the children as close to the start of the main axis as possible.

      This causes the safe effect as setting justifyContent to STRETCH then wrapping the LinearLayout in Align.left in case of horizontal layout or Align.top in case of vertical layout.

    • CENTER

      public static final LinearLayout.JustifyContent CENTER
      Place the children as close to the middle of the main axis as possible.

      This causes the safe effect as setting justifyContent to STRETCH then wrapping the LinearLayout in Align.hcenter in case of horizontal layout or Align.vcenter in case of vertical layout.

    • END

      public static final LinearLayout.JustifyContent END
      Place the children as close to the end of the main axis as possible.

      This causes the safe effect as setting justifyContent to STRETCH then wrapping the LinearLayout in Align.right in case of horizontal layout or Align.bottom in case of vertical layout.

    • SPACE_EVENLY

      public static final LinearLayout.JustifyContent SPACE_EVENLY
      The space will be distributed so that the spacing between any two items and the space to the edges are equal (along the main axis).

      If any child has a weight, the weights will be ignored.

    • SPACE_AROUND

      public static final LinearLayout.JustifyContent SPACE_AROUND
      Means that items are evenly distributed in the line with equal space around them. Note that visually the spaces aren’t equal, since all the items have equal space on both sides. The first item will have one unit of space against the container edge, but two units of space between the next item because that next item has its own spacing that applies.

      If any child has a weight, the weights will be ignored.

    • SPACE_BETWEEN

      public static final LinearLayout.JustifyContent SPACE_BETWEEN
      items are evenly distributed in the line; first item is on the start line, last item on the end line

      If any child has a weight, the weights will be ignored.
